review.why: Runs parallel browser sub-agents, one tab each, to build a cited Markdown and JSON report with a citation check.
review.summary: Splits a query into three to seven sub-questions, starts an isolated headless browser session, dispatches one sub-agent per sub-question, merges and deduplicates the findings, and renders a report with numbered sources. A drilldown mode adds a second wave. A check fails the run if any prose lacks a citation. It then closes tabs and the session.
strengths: Citation check fails the run when a sentence has no source
Uses a separate profile and socket so the user's own browser session is never touched
Cleanup rules keep pre-existing tabs and the user's session intact
cautions: Needs the openbrowser-ai command-line tool to be installed
Evidence is thin: a sub-agent keeps the page sentence that shares the most words with the question
Long procedure made of many shell blocks, and it scrapes search result pages
